blocks.text: The lacunary series f(x) = Σ x^(2ⁿ) obeys f(x) = x + f(x²). Along the specified dyadic path toward 1, subtracting k and a convergent constant leaves an explicit geometric tail.

blocks.label: Proved pathwise bound
blocks.text: The proof concerns xₖ = exp(−2⁻ᵏ). It does not establish the same additive constant for every boundary approach or the arithmetic nature of f(exp(−1)).

The double exponent 2ⁿ is essential. One index shift and elementary exponential bounds give the dyadic argument. The companion collapse note now proves Rₖ/(ζ(k) − 1) → 1 as integer k → ∞: this leading-ratio connection is established.

blocks.label: Scope of the limit
blocks.text: The bound proves f(xₖ) = k + C + O(2<super>−k</super>) along this specified dyadic approach to 1. It supplies no universal additive constant for every approach, and no algebraicity or transcendence classification of f(e<super>−1</super>).
